title: Unary first-argument oracle call
statement: Let $A$ be a register program, $o$ an oracle function, and $l,l_1,l_0$ control states. If the instruction at $l$ calls oracle $j$ in unary-first mode with the single argument register $r$ and branches to $l_1$ on true and $l_0$ on false, then on input encoding a unary word of length $n$ followed by a word $w$, one abstract step from state $l$, register assignment $v$, and no stored answer goes to $l_1$ exactly when $o(j,\langle 1^n,\mathrm{bits}(v(r))\rangle)$ is true, and otherwise goes to $l_0$, leaving the registers and stored answer unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: The instruction at l is the specified unary-first call to oracle j with the single register r and branch states l₁ and l₀
